cards.text: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon (Jeremiah 25:1). The army of the king of Babylon is besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet is NOT free to come and go.

cards.question: With Babylon's army besieging Jerusalem, where is Jeremiah the prophet locked up?

answers.text: In the courtyard of the guard
In the house of Jonathan the scribe

cards.text: That courtyard is in the palace of the king of Judah, and King Zedekiah is the one who locked him up there. Zedekiah says, 'Why are you prophesying like this?'

cards.question: Zedekiah says Jeremiah claims the LORD will deliver Jerusalem into the hand of the king of Babylon, and the king will ___ it.

cards.text: And it gets personal. Zedekiah won't escape: he'll be handed to the king of Babylon, see him eye to eye, and be taken to Babylon until the LORD attends to him.

cards.question: In Jeremiah's message, fighting against the Chaldeans will succeed.

cards.text: I guess when you don't like the forecast, you lock up the weatherman. But the forecasts keep coming: the LORD tells Jeremiah that Hanamel, the son of his uncle Shallum, is on his way to see him.

cards.question: The LORD says Jeremiah's cousin Hanamel will tell him he has the right of redemption to buy something. What is it?
Hanamel shows up in the courtyard of the guard, just as the LORD said he would.

cards.text: Babylon's army has the city surrounded, Jeremiah's under guard, and his cousin is URGING him to buy LAND. That's somebody selling you a beach house while the hurricane's pulling into the driveway.

cards.question: When Hanamel comes and asks, just as the LORD said, what does Jeremiah know?

answers.text: That this was the word of the LORD
That Hanamel was trying to trick him
That the siege was almost over

cards.text: So Jeremiah buys the field in Anathoth from his cousin Hanamel. He weighs out seventeen shekels of silver.

cards.question: Jeremiah makes the deal for the field quietly, with no witnesses around.

cards.text: Nope, he signs and seals the deed, calls in witnesses and weighs the silver on the scales. Then he takes the deed: the sealed copy with its terms and conditions, and the open copy.

cards.question: Jeremiah hands the deed to someone in front of Hanamel, the witnesses and all the Jews in the courtyard. Who gets it?

cards.text: Right there in front of everyone, Jeremiah instructs Baruch with a word from the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: take both copies of the deed and put them in a clay jar.

cards.question: Why does the LORD want both copies of the deed put in a clay jar?

answers.text: To preserve them for a long time
To hide them from the Chaldeans
To bury them out in the field

cards.question: Then the LORD of Hosts says why. Houses, fields and vineyards will ___ be bought in this land.

cards.text: I spent years in a drawer stuffed with receipts nobody would ever need, but THIS receipt gets its own clay jar. And that's where we leave it for now, friend, because this field's story isn't done.

findings.problem: The opening card copies verses 1 and 2 almost word for word, starting with "This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD." Apart from the capitalized NOT, it has none of Papa Dorin's voice. It reads like the verse text, not like Papa Dorin telling the story.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The Chaldeans first appear in verse 4. Card 5 leaves them out, and card 6 then asks about "fighting against the Chaldeans" without ever saying who they are. The baker has only heard of Babylon's army and the king of Babylon.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card retells the siege and Jeremiah being under guard, which come from verse 2. It cites only Jeremiah 32:8, so the citation is narrower than what the card tells.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Jeremiah actually pays for land in a city under siege, and the card gives that moment as a flat restatement of verse 9. Papa Dorin has no reaction or voice here, so the moment falls flat right after card 10 built it up.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Baruch first appears as the answer on card 15. Card 16 says Jeremiah instructs him, but no card ever says who Baruch is, for example Jeremiah's scribe (Jeremiah 36:4).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The last story card goes back to verse 14 (the clay jar) after card 18 has already covered verse 15. The joke is a recap that doesn't move the passage forward. Card 18 already asks about the last verse, so this card should be only the line that says the story isn't over, or the joke should move to a card that tells verse 14.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. When the passage's last verse is asked on a choice card, the last story card can be just this line.
